title.narrative: Provision of life-saving healthcare services as part of the response to the displacement across Syria

description.narrative: The protracted crisis snaps the multiple layers of the emergency have created a difficult humanitarian situation, with over 13 million people displaced within Syria and neighbouring countries after nearly 14 years of conflict. Approximately 16.9 million people remain in Syria, relying on humanitarian aid. An offensive launched on November 27, 2024, led to the government's overthrow on December 8, 2024. Since then, there have been multiple population movements, including displacement to safer areas from locations where the hostilities are still occurring; on the other hand, there has been an increase in the number of Syrian returnees, with an estimated 200,000 spontaneously returning from Lebanon, Jordan, and Turkey, according to UNHCR. These developments have intensified the existing emergency, adding new layers of need to an already dire humanitarian crisis.The health system is heavily disrupted, with just over 60% of hospitals and primary healthcare centres (PHCs) fully operational. This is primarily due to a lack of resources, including water and electricity, and shortages of healthcare workers. The cost of medicines and treatments is beyond the reach of most families. Additionally, the risk of disease outbreaks remains high as new arrivals seek refuge in overcrowded and inadequate shelters that often lack sufficient water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services. There is an urgent need to provide life-saving emergency health services across various response dynamics. Preparing for public health threats, particularly disease outbreaks, is critical as populations move.With support from CERF, WHO will immediately implement core emergency health interventions aimed at reducing avoidable morbidity and mortality among displaced populations and host communities through the following actions:1. Provision of essential medicines and medical supplies.2. Provision of essential primary and secondary healthcare services to ensure continuity of care for new arrivals and host communities.3. Disease surveillance and response.
